events.text: The maid sees Hyde beat Sir Danvers Carew to death with a cane.
events.quote: Mr. Hyde broke out of all bounds and clubbed him to the earth

events.text: The maid faints at the horror of the murder.
events.quote: At the horror of these sights and sounds, the maid fainted

events.text: The maid wakes at two and calls the police.
events.quote: It was two o’clock when she came to herself and called for the police

events.text: The victim's body is found mangled in the lane.
events.quote: there lay his victim in the middle of the lane, incredibly mangled

events.text: A sealed envelope addressed to Utterson is found on the victim.
events.quote: which bore the name and address of Mr. Utterson

events.text: Utterson identifies the body as Sir Danvers Carew.
events.quote: I am sorry to say that this is Sir Danvers Carew

events.text: The officer narrates the maid's account and shows the broken stick.
events.quote: he briefly narrated what the maid had seen, and showed the broken stick

events.text: Utterson recognizes the stick as one he gave Henry Jekyll.
events.quote: he recognised it for one that he had himself presented many years before to Henry Jekyll

events.text: Utterson offers to take the officer to Hyde's house.
events.quote: I think I can take you to his house

events.text: The old woman lets Utterson and the inspector search Hyde's rooms.
events.quote: we wish to see his rooms

events.text: They find the other half of the stick and a burnt cheque book.
events.quote: the other half of the stick was found behind the door

events.text: The inspector finds several thousand pounds to Hyde's credit at the bank.
events.quote: several thousand pounds were found to be lying to the murderer’s credit

events.text: The inspector plans to wait for Hyde at the bank and issue handbills.
events.quote: We have nothing to do but wait for him at the bank, and get out the handbills
